fact: Stored paths are followed only on this computer or the drawing's own network share; UNC paths to other hosts, file://host URLs, device paths and URL schemes are refused with a reason and treated like a missing file
correction: The claim is correct in substance; precise wording: Paths stored in a drawing (xref paths and table data links) are resolved only through craft_docpath (pinned at craft-libs rev 82a24b0 in /home/user/cadcraft_1/Cargo.toml), a lexical, no-I/O check. A relative stored path is taken from the drawing's folder; a UNC path is followed only when its host and share equal the drawing's own share (compared ignoring ASCII case), otherwise it is refused as Refused::Network ("the path is on another computer"). file: URLs with a non-local host (anything but an empty host or "localhost") are refused as Network, while file:///path, file://localhost/path and file:///C:/... are accepted as local paths. Device paths (\\.\, \\?\ non-drive, \??\, and DOS reserved names such as CON, NUL, COM1 with or without extension) are refused as Refused::Device ("the path names a device, not a file"); non-file URL schemes (http, https, smb, webdav, mailto, data, javascript, ms-word, ...) are refused as Refused::Url ("the link is not a file path"); empty/control-character/above-root paths, and relative paths when the drawing has no file, are Refused::Invalid. Consequences: an xref with a refused path is not loaded, its block stays empty, and its status is XrefStatus::Unresolved (not NotFound) with the log line "<path>: not opened, <reason>"; -XREF ? shows no foundAt, XOPEN fails with the reason, and reload follows the saved path the same way. As with a genuinely missing file, the loader still looks for a file of the same name beside the host drawing, so a same-named local copy can satisfy a refused xref path. A refused table data link is reported as a per-link error "<path>: not opened, <reason>" and nothing is read (no fallback). Paths the user types (XATTACH, -XREF Path, DATALINK) are used as given. The behaviour is documented only in code comments and the craft-libs README; no cadcraft docs/ page mentions it, and the craftrules standards repo could not be checked (not accessible from this session).

finding: Keep the copy-on-write EntityStore (Arc chunks of 1024, sharded handle index): snapshots, undo, autosave and spatial caches are pointer copies, and it is the natural substrate for sharing a loaded reference between host, palette and caches without copying. subject: Deterministic copy between drawings
finding: Keep the merge rules verbatim: existing named definitions in the target win, anonymous * blocks get fresh generated names, nested blocks and record-to-record dependencies (layer->linetype, dimstyle->textstyle) travel with the objects, new handles, source drawing uid tracked for Paste-to-original. CADCraft implements this three times (clipboard, insert-from-file, import); Genesis should have one merge_definitions used by paste, insert, import, bind and packaging. Change: add a stable per-object GUID so re-pasting the same source object is an idempotent update, return a merge report (kept/renamed/dropped) as the command result for users and agents, and remap handles to preserve dimension associativity when both ends were copied (CADCraft always drops it). Keep DXF text as the cross-process clipboard format.

subject: Crash-proofing
finding: Keep everything: deny lints for unwrap/expect/panic plus forbid(unsafe), Result everywhere, catch_unwind at every boundary (command, interactive step, prompt/preview, open, file read, DWG bridge, LISP, render thread) with restore from the pre-command Arc<Drawing>, non-finite refusal, the hostile_* test convention plus a cross-command hostile_params_never_panic, caps on every input-sized loop, background autosave with lock files and tmp+rename, immediate autosave on GPU fault, GPU errors captured by callbacks. Add what CADCraft lacks: a CI gate running the full check on every PR (its S1 gap is why it self-scores stability 35% despite the architecture), an append-only command journal per drawing so recovery replays to the last action rather than the last 10-minute autosave, web autosave (IndexedDB), a DWG path that does not inflate 6x into DXF text (#57 is the one crash-adjacent failure users reported), reader fuzzing, and opt-in crash/hang telemetry so 'zero crashes' is measurable.

fact: Vertical alignments and corridors exist in BricsCAD civil tools and require projection; horizontal alignments import from LandXML and Civil 3D
correction: Correct but incomplete. Precise wording: In BricsCAD Pro's Civil tools, vertical alignments (built by placing PVIs on the TIN-surface profile under a horizontal alignment, viewed with ALIGNMENTVIEW) and corridors (CORRIDOR command: a corridor template swept along a 3D alignment or string, or a 'simple corridor' along horizontal-alignment PI points on a TIN surface) both exist, and both require the horizontal alignment to first be projected (draped) onto a TIN surface ("Projection is required to create Vertical Alignments and Corridors"). Alignments can be imported two ways: LANDXMLIMPORT brings in Horizontal Alignments (by PI and by Elements), 3D Alignments, TIN surfaces, civil points and strings, and imported LandXML vertical alignments automatically create 3D Alignments; CIVIL3DIMPORT reads a Civil 3D DWG (or converts the current drawing) and imports Alignments (by PI and by Elements) AND Profiles (vertical alignments), plus COGO points, point groups, TIN/volume/grid surfaces and profile views. So it is not only horizontal alignments that import; vertical alignments/profiles do too. Minor caveats: LANDXMLIMPORT is documented as not available on Linux, and corridors themselves are not imported (they are rebuilt in BricsCAD from a template plus 3D alignment).

correction: Correct in substance, but imprecise. Precise wording: In a January 2025 Bricsys forum thread ("Panning and crashing"), a user running BricsCAD V25.1.07-1 (Civil/survey workflow, small drawing of survey points, linework and a few blocks) reported a fatal error while panning or zooming. A second user on the same build reported black-screen crashes when panning/zooming on an AMD Pro WX3200 / Ryzen 5600 system and said support had not been able to help them, so MTFLAGS=0 was a diagnostic step that resolved one reported case, not a universally confirmed or officially documented fix. MTFLAGS is Bricsys's bit-coded multithreading flag (default 3015; 0 = no parallel processing of display and loading). V25.1.07 shipped 16 Dec 2024 and its release notes contain no pan/zoom crash fix; a related but narrower crash ("crash when panning while drawing annotative dimensions") was fixed earlier in V25.1.06.

fact: 2010 ADA Standards Table 208.2 scopes accessible spaces by lot size and one in six accessible spaces must be van-accessible
correction: Correct in substance, imprecise in wording. Precise version: 2010 ADA Standards section 208.2 / Table 208.2 ("Parking Spaces") sets the minimum number of accessible spaces based on the "Total Number of Parking Spaces Provided in Parking Facility" -- i.e. the count of spaces (not physical lot area), calculated separately for each parking facility (lot or structure), not on the site-wide total. Rows: 1-25 -> 1; 26-50 -> 2; 51-75 -> 3; 76-100 -> 4; 101-150 -> 5; 151-200 -> 6; 201-300 -> 7; 301-400 -> 8; 401-500 -> 9; 501-1000 -> 2 percent of total; 1001 and over -> 20 plus 1 for each 100, or fraction thereof, over 1000 (separate percentages apply to hospital outpatient 10%, rehab/outpatient PT 20%, and residential facilities under 208.2.1-208.2.3). Section 208.2.4 Van Parking Spaces: "For every six or fraction of six parking spaces required by 208.2 to comply with 502, at least one shall be a van parking space complying with 502" -- so the 1-in-6 ratio counts required accessible spaces (not total spaces), rounds up ("or fraction of six"), and always yields at least one van space. Note: DOJ's restriping brief table reads "500 to 1000" where the Standards say "501 to 1000".
